newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU silent on which countries set to join EMU.
newsitem.headline: EU silent on which countries set to join EMU.

text.p: The European Commission has not made any comments on which countries are likely to qualify for economic and monetary union (EMU) from its planned start in 1999, a Commission spokesman said on Monday.
However, he noted that the economic forecasts the European Union executive put forward in May seemed to be holding up.
The forecasts listed seven countries as meeting the Maastricht treaty's criterion of a budget deficit of no more than three percent of Gross Domestic Prodcut in 1997.

Those countries were Denmark, Germany, France, Ireland, Luxembourg, the Netherlands and Finland. Sweden and Austria were expected to have deficits of 3.1 percent, just over the limit. The forecast was made under the assumption of unchanged policies.

Economic Affairs Commissioner Yves-Thibault de Silguy said in Dublin on Saturday, "The timetable for the single curency will be respected and participation in EMU is within grasp for an important number of member states from 1999."
The deficit criterion is one of four requirements for joining monetary union as laid down in the Maastricht treaty. The others concern debt levels, interest rates, currency stability and inflation.
